utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, would you please have the accused brought in? (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, first let me check and see whether the interpretation is operational, I hope everyone is off to a good week? Everyone can hear me? Office of the Prosecutor, you can hear me; Defence you hear me as well? General Blaskic, you can hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLASKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour, I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Great, thank you. I would suggest that we get going. I see that the protective measures have been set up. Mr. Harmon, go right ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning your Honours, good morning counsel. Mr. President, our next witness is a protected witness and he has requested facial protection only. He is named Adnan Zec and he will be testifying to your Honours this morning about his observations that he saw before the attack on 16th April. He will describe to your Honours his observations of the bungalow, he will describe his observations at the school that he attended and observations of local Croats leaving the village before the attack took place. He will also testify about the Territorial Defence to the extent that his father was a participant in it. Then we will turn, Mr. President, to the events on 16th April, in lower Ahmici. Adnan Zec will describe the murder of innocent civilians, troop concentrations that he observed in lower Ahmici, the different units that he could identify participating in a co-ordinated fashion in the attack. He will testify about the destruction of the mosque in lower Ahmici. He will testify about looting by the HVO, intentional fire setting of residents of Muslim residences, and he will testify about the lack of resistance by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, you have described this very well. So for the time being at first we are going to begin by introducing the witness, so Registrar, could you lower the blinds that we could show the witness in and then we will raise the blinds so that the people in the gallery can follow the proceedings. So it is just facial protection you are talking about, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I make an observation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We do not wish to delay the proceedings, but we wish to note that as a matter of principle, unless there is a specific basis for a protective measure, where a witness has gone out in the media and made himself a public figure by granting interviews and having his face photographed and printed in the media, we think there should be some kind of factual basis for the court to grant protective measures. We do not wish this individual to be in any kind of harm's way and we refer to the court's good discretion and judgement in this area, but we wish to bring that to the court's attention and to state our principle view with respect to the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before deciding this, I would like to hear what the Office of the Prosecutor has to say. When was that interview given, Mr. Harmon? Is this a recent interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the interview that counsel has just showed you is a copy of an interview that I provided to counsel recently in discovery. When it came to my attention I provided it to him. Counsel is correct, there is I believe a picture of the witness in there, but nevertheless, Mr. President, I am prepared to make a showing today to your Honours of the threats that have been made to this young man. If the court wishes to go into private session I will be happy to have him describe the threats that have been made to him that have caused him sufficient fear that he no longer wants to have his face shown in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What we are going to do is when the witness is in the courtroom we will ask him the conditions under which he gave that interview. It is quite right what Mr. Hayman says, it is difficult to ask for strict protective measures from the Tribunal. Of course, it is the Tribunal's duty to protect witnesses, we do that as and when necessary, but the witnesses themselves have to see to their own protection. Thank you, Mr. Harmon, thank you, counsel for the Prosecution. Let us bring in the witness, please, usher. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me? The first thing you have to tell the usher, Mr. Registrar, is to put the headset at the disposal of the witness, otherwise -- can you hear me? Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You do, great. You are going to tell us your first and last name and then you will stand and read out the solemn oath please. What is your name, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Adnan Zec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please stand and read the solemn declaration which all witnesses are bound to read. If you would please stand, sir? Please read that oath, sir. MR. ADNAN ZEC (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Zec, we will see exactly how your name is spelt, but in any event, Mr. Zec -- could you spell that please for me, the interpreters? Z-E-C, Mr. Zec. That is how it is pronounced, is it? I will work it out in the end. Mr. Zec, you are subject to the protective measures ordered by the court, you have asked that there be facial protection for you, that has been provided, but we have just learnt you had given an interview in a publication. We do not want to spend much time on this, but you did think it was appropriate to give this interview, do not say too much about it, which may lead to revealing matters relevant to your identity that you do not want everyone to know, but everyone has to help out when it comes to protection, including the witnesses themselves. So Office of the Prosecutor, now you have called this witness, you have perfectly outlined the main points of the testimony that your Office is expecting to hear, so perhaps after some basic identification, we will ask the witness to testify. Of course, we have our expedited procedure, as it were, so please interrupt as little as possible except when there are points of clarification you would like to dwell on and then you can have questions afterwards which you think are vital to the case of the Prosecution. So Mr. Harmon, if you need to go into any questions concerning identification, please do so. Thereafter, the witness will go into the areas that you have outlined. Please proceed, Mr. Harmon. Examined by MR. HARMON

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will start by asking him some questions about identification and then I will ask him some brief questions about a selected number of topics and then I will ask him to go into his narrative, with the court's permission. Adnan, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am now 18 and I was 13 in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you raised all of your life in the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me be turn your attention to 15th April 1993. Did you attend school on 15th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, unusual did you notice when you went to school on 15th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that certain Croatian children, children of Croatian extraction, were not attending school, especially the children from Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you normally take a bus to school and back from school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that bus normally pass the location known as the bungalow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the bus was coming from Turbe, from the direction of Vitez, then would turn around in Nadioci and go back to Vitez. I would get on the bus in Ahmici and then would go to Vitez to go to school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the bus would go past Ahmici, continue on the road toward Busovaca until it hit a turn-out after it passed the bungalow and then it would return to Vitez, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the judges about the bungalow, please, what it was and what you saw at the bungalow at various times before the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bungalow was a restaurant of sorts. However, about a month before 15th April, the military arrived in two or three buses and they took up their quarters there. There was machine-gun nest right next to it, and the soldiers wore camouflage uniforms, and weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many soldiers did you see at the bungalow the month before the attack on Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately there were about 70 soldiers stationed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those soldiers were in camouflage uniforms, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to school on 15th April 1993, did you also see the bungalow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on 15th April I did see the bungalow. There was no bus on that day. When I arrived in a bus, there were about seven or eight soldiers outside, and whenever I would pass by there, somebody would always be in this machine-gun nest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bungalow and the soldiers you are talking about were Croats, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, did I interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had the HV insignia on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: HV is from -- what does that represent, "HV"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: HV is the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on 15th April, Adnan, you saw a smaller number of soldiers in and around the bungalow, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you returned home from school on 15th April, did you see anything unusual or did you hear about any unusual activities that had taken place in and around your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I returned, my parents were commenting on why these children from Ahmici did not go to school that day. They saw them around on that day. Then the Milicevic family, these are three households, three families, they had driven their families away in cars, and in front of Ivo Papic's house, different vehicles were constantly coming and going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Milicevic family is Croat and the Papic family you mentioned are also Croats, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This individual by the name of Papic, what was his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragan Papic, Goran and Ivo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did he live across the road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I thought that we had said certain things, if you recall, I think we have prepare -- you have prepared the witness and maybe we could let the witness get on with his narrative. I know you have some reluctance to go along with this procedure, I think, but I do think that we had agreed that we would try to stick to the essentials of the case. It is perhaps appropriate for you to put a few questions, but I think you were back in the former way of doing things, as it were. I would like the witness to testify before the court, so maybe you could have a few more questions, but I would like to get on with that procedure. Maybe we could have a mix of the methods, as it were, counsel, but here I think we are back to you putting the hundreds of questions you have worked out with the witness and I think we have seen that hundreds of questions, they are not all essential to the case, so let us try to work on this approach. Please proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the court's indulgence I only have a few more questions and then I intend to have the witness commence on his narrative, but I need to set the stage for the witness's testimony in order to put it clearly to the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So you have the court's indulgence. Go right ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Adnan, on 16th April 1993, who was living with you at your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father, Sabahudin Zec, he was 37 years old; my mother, Hajrija Zec, who was 40 years old; my sister Alisa Zec, who was 11 years old, and my sister Melisa, who was 6 years old; and myself, who was 13 at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few questions about your father. Your father was a member of the TO, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your father participated on occasion walking around the village as part of a village guard, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your father participated as a member of the village guard, did he have a gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the village had some hunting rifles and some other weapons which were handmade, and that is what they were using and that is how they were guarding the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 16th April, the morning of the attack, were there any weapons at all in your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now with the court's permission, with the usher's assistance, I would like to have Prosecutor's Exhibit 141 disseminated and I would like one copy of Prosecutor's Exhibit 141 placed in front of the witness. For the record, Mr. President, 141 is an enlargement of a portion of Exhibit 50, it is a map and attached thereto is a legend which identifies the various numbers and letters that are identified on the photograph itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Counsel, what about the legend here, the title, is that covered by the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. Adnan, before coming into court today did you have the opportunity to locate on a large aerial image a number of locations that are relevant to your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those locations marked with numbers and letters on Prosecutor's Exhibit 141 that is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to compare the legend that is attached to that exhibit with the numbers and letters that are found on Prosecutor's Exhibit 141?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the legend accurately correspond to the letters and numbers and locations described therein?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Adnan, using that exhibit when you feel it necessary, to illustrate what you will be telling the judges, can you please tell the judges what happened to you and to members of your family on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, counsel. I think that is the way forward. So you have heard what the Prosecutor has just told you, you are going to testify about all the elements that are relevant for the case of the Prosecution and when you think it is appropriate to do so, you point out the areas that are germane. If you forget to say something, then do not worry, the Prosecutor will put a few questions to you and everything will be cleared up. Now please speak in your own words and testify, tell us what happened, beginning by responding to the question just put to you by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15th April, in the evening around 9.00 or 10.00, we all went to bed. In the morning, the following morning, very early, around --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you could speak a bit louder please, or move closer to the microphone, because otherwise the interpreters have a tough time hearing you. Thank you. Please do move forward. Just relax, do relax, speak calmly and near the microphone. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning around 5.00 or 5.30, we were awakened by shooting. The bullets were smashing the windows and the roof tiles. I was sleeping in one room, my two sisters in another and my parents, my father and my mother, in the third bedroom. The parents ran out of their bedroom towards us, to wake us up, so that we could get dressed and we could run away, because we had to put on some clothes and the house was already on fire. We were in the pyjamas and we ran out and at first we stayed in the hallway on the upper floor of our house. We could not stay there, then we went to the ground floor under the staircase. We only took the clothes that we could put on and while we were under the staircase, the parents agreed that they would go back to the top floor and take the money and gold, so that we could take it with us. My mother went upstairs and she screamed. We thought that she may have been hit. However, she was not hit, the bullet had hit the room and it was a bullet that set the room on fire, and so she screamed and she put out the fire, she took the money and the gold and came back to us downstairs. When she came back, in fact my parents again talked it through and they agreed that we should leave the house, because the house was very soon going to be all on fire and we did not want to be burned in the house, so they decided that we should go to the house, Zijad Ahmic's house, which is marked with number 5. That is the house that is set a little bit into the ground so it has a kind of a basement. So we tried to wait it out a little bit so that the shooting would subside. However the shooting never subsided, so we decided to run out of the house and run up to the other house. At first, my little sister Melisa and mama ran out, then my sister Alisa, then myself and then my father. I was running in the direction of -- along this road marked in red (indicates), and my parents along the green road. When I came to Nurija's house, this is house marked with 3, I took shelter behind the upper side of the house so that I could rest. Then at the moment I turned the corner, there was a burst of tracer bullets coming from below. It came in the direction where I was just running a moment ago. As I was at Nurija's house, my parents were above our barn, which is marked with number 2. After I rested a bit there, I continued to run. I ran to the area of about Zahir's house, and again I could feel that a burst of fire was shot immediately next to me and I threw myself to the ground. When I saw that I was not hit, I got up and continued to run. When I came out to the road itself, and this is where this red arrow makes a curve (indicates), I continued another ten to fifteen metres along that path, and I saw a soldier who was standing next to Zahir's house. This is marked with A. That is where he was standing. It was one soldier who told me, "where are you going, kid?". I said that I was running because of the shooting and he said, "run along". However, next to him, Zahir was already lying on the ground. He had no weapons on him, he was dressed in civilian clothes and as I said, this soldier in camouflage uniform was standing over him and he also was -- had his face painted in black. I continued to run to the cross road, which is marked with C, and the soldiers -- in fact there were three soldiers who were at the spot marked by letter B, and as I had to pass them on the way to Zijad Ahmic's house, which was marked with 5, as I had to pass by them, they also stopped me and asked, "where are you going, kid?", and I responded that I was running because there was shooting, but they said, "no, stop, go back". Since I was very close to them, maybe a metre away from them, I turned around and started running back. However, as I turned around, and I may have made one or two steps, a burst of fire was shot at me and I fell down. The three soldiers who were in the spot marked with B, while I was running in the direction towards them, as I was approaching them, they were intermittently coming out and going back as if they were hiding from someone and they were shooting in the direction of Gornji Selo, but they were hidden, they were crouching behind -- the place where they were was a place where some kind of a shed or a barn was standing, but that is where they were hiding behind, they were crouching and then occasionally they would come out and they would shoot at the upper village. The one who shot at me was the first to the right, and he was the one who ordered the soldier who was in a location marked with A to shoot at my parents. When I was hit, in fact when I was about to hit the ground, I saw that my parents were arriving at the position marked with D. They came to a stop there and they were killed by the soldier at A, who received the order from this soldier by whom I was shot. He told him and repeated this three times, "kill them, kill them, kill them". When he said, "kill them" for the second time, my parents -- in fact my father said, "kill me and let my wife and children go", but for the third time, he got the order and he shot two bursts of fire which killed my parents. As I fell down there, I felt my leg going numb, and I saw that I was hit in the leg. I was shot in two different places. I did not dare move because the soldiers were right next to me so I remained lying there all day. I put my arms over my face so that they would not notice that I was alive, simply not to see any movement, because they were coming over to me. The soldiers would come to me and would crouch by me and would shoot at the upper village, so I had to do this so they would not notice that I would move my eye lids. So I had to keep my arm over my eyes and in this way, I was also able to observe what was going on around me. Further on during the day, soldiers kept going by me because this seemed to be their main thoroughfare, so to speak, they kept coming and going there. They were coming from the house of Pjanic, Habiba Pjanic, marked number 4, from my house marked as number 1, and from those two directions, they were come and then they would go different ways towards Zijad's house, number 5 and further on along the road towards the mosque, but I do not know how far they would get up there. They would keep coming back and going and they were coming and going back a lot. During the day, I do not know what time it was, I heard in Zahir's house that there were refugees living there downstairs. I forget where they were from exactly, but I heard them being driven out. When they drove them out, they told them that they had to put their hands on their heads and they shot dead one of these people, one of these refugees, a man, I cannot remember his name though. That is letter G. So he was executed right in front of the house. The rest of them, his wife and two children, were driven away, I saw that. I saw him when he was forced out of the house and when he was ordered to put his hands on his head and I noticed that they would actually shoot him then so I closed my eyes and then I heard a burst of gunfire and he probably fell, I did not see him fall, but I think it can be assumed. His wife and two children were driven away, they went by me. I heard them walking, I heard their steps. I was not watching, I was afraid, I had my eyes closed so I just heard them walking and I heard their sighs. They went by me and further on during the day, they carried a wounded person by me on a stretcher. That direction is not exactly depicted here, but they carried this wounded person by and as they walked up to me, they said, "is this one of our guys?", but one of the men carrying the stretchers said "no", and they went on. Also during that day, Andjelko Vidovic, whose nickname was Acko, went by me with a few soldiers towards the house of Trako Mehemed and Trako Zilka. We have not marked this house, though. When they went further up, I heard them banging at the door, they even broke a window. I heard a scream. I heard his wife Zilka scream, then also a burst of gunfire. At that point, I thought that Zilka was hit and I thought she must have been shot dead, but after that, I found out that it was Mehemed Trako who was killed. In the afternoon, before dusk perhaps, I sort of fell asleep. I do not know if I really fell asleep or whether I simply fainted, I cannot remember that, but I was simply awakened by a lot of noise, the clamour of soldiers who were standing next to me when I opened my eyes, there were 20 or 30 of them altogether. Then at Almir's shed, some of them were trying actually to breakdown the door of the garage where the car was. They wanted to torch it. Others were protesting, saying that it should not be torched, but he did set it on fire after all and one of them was talking into a radio. I could not see him because I did not dare open my eyes, I was afraid that they would notice I was alive, because they were simply standing next to me. At that particular cross road, they were talking into the radio transmitter and saying, "are you advancing in the village of Pirici? Do you need reinforcements? There are plenty of us over here. Send us explosives for the lower mosque in Ahmici". After he said that, I do not know if I had moved a little or perhaps they had noticed me moving before that or maybe they noticed that I was breathing, one of them said, "this kid is alive, he is breathing" and he was pointing at me. Then I already felt that I was dead, I was simply expecting him to fire at me and kill me and finish me off. However, one of them walked up to me, touched me a bit with his foot, kicked me a bit, turned me around a bit and he said, "no, he is dead, he is not alive". He said something to that effect. After that, they went towards Zilka Trako's house and towards Zijad's house, while Elvir's shed was already burning. I decided to get up. I was all wet. There was a drizzle that day, not a lot of rain, but I was all wet nevertheless and I wanted to get dry. I got up and tried to leave, but I was very dizzy when I stood up, as if I had had a lot of alcohol to drink. I tried to steady myself by holding the gate that was open while they were carrying that wounded person by me, so I held the gate for a while and then I staggered towards Elvir's barn, and I managed to get to Elvir's barn, where the fire was burning, actually. When I got up from this place where I had been lying, I saw up there by Zilka's house, or rather by the shed and towards Zijad's house, I mean in that direction, I saw soldiers walking up there. Actually the barn was burning, so I did not know whether it had been torched then or beforehand, but it was on fire. When I reached the barn, I could not really stand, so I lay down on the ground and I moved a bit from the barn so that the roof would not fall on me, and I fell asleep there. I woke up some time during the night or perhaps it was already morning, I cannot remember what woke me up, the detonation from the mosque or the heat that was coming from there, because when I woke up, I was very very hot. The roof had already fallen off, everything was on fire but I was not on fire. I got up and I went to the house of Ahmic Elvir, or Ahmic Mirsad rather, which is marked number 6. Mr. Harmon, do you want to ask me something at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I have a number of questions that I would like to ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Counsel, we have heard the testimony of the witness, we thank him for it. Now what we expect from you, Mr. Harmon, is not to go through all the questions again, otherwise that would be pointless as well as it would be unnecessary suffering on the part of the witness. Having said that, I think it is perfectly legitimate that you put the questions which you think are essential to your case. Go right ahead, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness -- I will ask him a number of questions and then the witness will continue with his narrative because he has not concluded his narrative, but there are a number of points that need to be clarified and let me proceed then with those clarifications. Adnan, you said you came very close to a soldier who was the single soldier next to the body of Zahir Ahmic. How was that soldier dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform on. He had black paint on his face, something black on his face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any insignia on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had insignia, but I am not sure what insignia, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have an eagle on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had an eagle on his uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that eagle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the left-hand side of his chest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now Adnan, let me turn your attention to the three soldiers who you next came into contact with. Were they in camouflage uniforms as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they also had camouflage uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have an eagle on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure whether they had an eagle or a joker on their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you also see patches with the letters HV on those particular soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, during the day as I lay there, many soldiers passed by me and I saw them wearing HV insignia and I also saw soldiers in black uniforms. I mean they were dressed in black, everything they wore was black, and they also had full gear and I also noticed the Vitezovi patch, but I cannot remember on what uniforms there was a Vitezovi patch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Adnan, just focusing on the three soldiers who were involved in the killing of your family, I just want to focus on the insignia that were on those soldiers. Were HV patches on those soldiers or were they on different soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were wounded. Can you describe your wounds to the judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one bullet hit the upper part of my left leg, my thigh, and another bullet hit the heel of my left foot and it went out on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to turn your attention to the moment when your parents were killed. You saw them executed, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they were running in your direction at the time they were shot, were they with your two sisters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they holding your two sisters at the time they were shot by these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father was holding the hand of my sister Alisa and my mother was holding the hand of my sister Melisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Alisa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two bursts of gunfire were shot at them, one burst of gunfire hit my father and my sister Alisa, and the other burst of gunfire only hit my mother, while my sister Melisa was not hit. She simply fainted, she fell on to the ground together with my mother, but she was not hit really, my sister Melisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your sister Alisa was killed at the same time your father was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Adnan, at the time your mother was killed, she was wearing a dress, was she not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she wore a red house dress, a house coat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was your father dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father wore jeans and he only had a sweater, I think. He did not even have a jacket on. My sister Alisa was wearing a skirt; my sister Melisa also wore trousers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the three soldiers who were involved in the killing of your parents have a walkie-talkie with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the one who shot at me had a walkie-talkie, and during the day I heard him saying something into it a few times, but I did not manage to understand what he was saying, and as far as I could tell, he was some kind of superior to all of them, because during the day, he would tell the soldiers, "why are you going there? Go over here". He would curse at them, swear at their mothers et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now with the assistance of the usher, if I could have Exhibit 116/2 placed on the ELMO? Mr. Usher, if you could also take 100/2 as well with you to the ELMO it would be much faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Counsel, the exhibit here that the witness was referring to, what was the number on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 141, Mr. President, and we will be returning to that exhibit with the narrative of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would assume that could be entered into evidence without any objection on the part of the Defence. All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could place 116/2 on the ELMO. Adnan, you said you observed a number of patches while you were laying on the pathway. I am showing you Exhibit 116/2. Do you recognise that particular patch and is that patch similar to what you saw soldiers wearing on April 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is similar to the patch I saw on 16th April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me have placed Exhibit 100/2 on the ELMO, and ask you, Adnan, is this patch one of the patches that you also saw on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is also the patch I saw on 16th April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I am finished with those exhibits. If 141, the enlargement of the photograph, could be placed again on the ELMO, I would appreciate it. Adnan, you saw soldiers wearing patches that were with an eagle, you saw patches that were Joker patches and insignia, you saw HVO patches, you saw men in black uniforms and you saw men in camouflage uniforms. Did it appear to you while you lay on the ground throughout that day that the soldiers wearing those various uniforms and insignia were working together in a co-ordinated fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it seemed that they were all working together as if they were mixed together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question about heavier weapons that you heard being fired on 16th April. Did you hear an anti-aircraft gun being fired at all that day, while you were laying there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that day, when I was lying at the location marked as C, so that is the cross-roads, I heard from house number 4, the house of Habiba Pjanic, I heard some voices coming from there. I tried to move then, because I was fed up, I could not lie that way all the time. I went all numb, so I tried to move on my elbows, but I managed to move only about ten to twenty centimetres. From the direction of Habiba's house, I heard a burst of gunfire. It was not an ordinary burst of gunfire, it was very loud. From guns, it was not that loud, so I could hear there was a difference, a difference in sound. So this burst of gunfire that came from the direction of Pjanic's house, I was on my elbows and this burst of gunfire went very high up, about a metre above me, it hit the house of Hidajet, I cannot remember his last name, but the house has not been marked all that well either. So that is how the house was set on fire. Part of it hit the iron fence that was above me, and these bullets ricocheted and went by me and hit the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let me ask you some questions about your observations. You said you saw a male refugee who had his hands above his head shot by some soldiers. What kind of uniforms were those soldiers wearing who executed the Muslim refugee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms, they had camouflage uniforms and they also had black paint on their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw some soldiers go towards the direction and toward the house of Zilka Trako and that you later learned that Mehemed Trako was murdered. What kind of uniforms did those soldiers have on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mehemed Trako a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was a Muslim and he was a distant relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were laying on the ground, did you see your house being set afire and can you please explain to the judges what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As I lay there that morning, it was quite early, three soldiers came, I think they were in camouflage uniforms, they stayed in the house for a short while and then they went out. Soon after they got out, thick smoke started coming out of the house, so the house was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to turn your attention very briefly to the 20 or 30 soldiers who were standing next to you and who were in some form of radio communication about Pirici and about the mosque. Did you ever see what kind of uniforms those soldiers had on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That evening, when that noise woke me up, I opened my eyes only for a little, a very little, because there were a lot of people there, 20 or 30 soldiers. I am not sure whether they only had camouflage uniforms or whether there were camouflage and black uniforms there, because I closed my eyes. I was afraid they would notice I was alive and that they would kill me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 16th, before you sought refuge in the house of Elvir Ahmic, can you estimate how many soldiers you saw passing by you throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During that day, I saw at least 100 soldiers, because they were passing by me non-stop, going up and down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Adnan, if you would now please continue with your narrative, describing to the judges what happened once you got inside --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps before we proceed with the witness's narrative, I do not know how long it is going to be as far as the second part goes, but it might be appropriate to take a break. It is 11.10 and we will resume at 11.30. The court stands adjourned. (11.10 am) (A short break) (11.30 am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The court is back in session. Please bring in the accused, Mr. Registrar. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, we are now going to be hearing the second part of the testimony of the witness. Now, the Chamber will be adjourning at 12.30 and then we will be resuming at 2.45 pm this afternoon. Adnan, you are going to go ahead as you did this morning and then the counsel for the Prosecution will be putting questions to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Adnan, would you please then continue with your narrative. Tell the judges what happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I entered the house of Mirsad Ahmic, which is marked with the number 6, that house was on fire. The walls were very hot, I started going upstairs. I was walking up the staircase to the landing leading to the upper floor, so that is the part where the steps stop and then they continued on upstairs. When I got there, I was too dizzy to make it all the way up, so I decided to lie down there. So I lay down and I simply lost consciousness. I was unconscious for two days and two nights, and after two days and two nights I came to. It was early in the morning, it had not dawned yet, and in front of my eyes, I was seeing the images of these mass killings, those images were coming back, and the image of the entire village on fire. I waited until the dawn broke, and I then climbed to the upper floor of the house. From the top floor, I did not move from there at all, I was there for eight days, in fact I only left it on the eighth day. During the time that I spent in the house of Mirsad Ahmic, marked as number 6, I saw many dead bodies. I saw my own family, which is marked with letter D; I saw Husein Ahmic, who is marked with letter F, that is an older man, maybe 55 years of age; I also saw Zahir, who is marked with letter E; I saw two -- I do not know who they were, but they were civilians, and they are marked with letter I. Since the distance was a bit greater there, I could only notice that they were civilians. I also saw Mineta Ahmic, who is marked with H, she was lying in a barn. The door was ajar so that from the window, I could observe that this was Mineta. Next to her, I saw someone else, but I was not sure who that was, but there was someone else next to her and later I learned, after I had made my way out, I found out that it was her son, Semir, who was eight years old. That is Semir Ahmic. During the time I was in this house, the Milicevic family --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Adnan, before I interrupt you, before you proceed with the rest of your narrative, I would like to show you two exhibits. If they could be placed on the ELMO successively, Mr. President, the first would be Exhibit 142 and the next exhibit, if the usher could take that with him to the ELMO, would be Exhibit 136/1. If we could start with the small exhibit, 142, and place that on the ELMO, Mr. President and counsel, 142 is also accompanied by a legend which the witness has had an opportunity to inspect and confirm the accuracy of the A, B and C letters on 142.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Adnan, what has been placed on the ELMO in front of you is Prosecutor's Exhibit 142, and starting with the letter A, is that the house of Mirsad Ahmic, the house where you were hiding during those number of days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the house with the letter B, is that your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the letter C is the house of Nurija Ahmic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your family was executed somewhere between your house, which is letter B, and the house indicated by the letter A, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, between our house and Mirsad's house and Zahir's house, which cannot be seen because it is blocked by the view of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now Mr. Usher if you could place Prosecutor's Exhibit 136/1 on the ELMO, Adnan, this is an exhibit that was previously introduced last week. The house on the left, do you recognise that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The house that is a little bit off centre to the right, is that also the house of Nurija Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your narrative testimony just a few minutes ago, you indicated that you had seen two civilian bodies and those are indicated at location I on Prosecutor's Exhibit 141. You see in the Exhibit 136/1 there are a number of bodies that are next to your house; can you see that in that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those bodies, given their location, were those bodies visible from your hiding place in Mirsad Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Adnan, those bodies are different from the bodies that are located at point I on Prosecutor's Exhibit 141; those are other bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher, I am finished with those exhibits. Adnan, would you please continue then with your narrative.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the following days which I spent in this house (indicates), the Milicevic family, they are marked with number 8, they returned their families to their homes, because on 15th April they had taken them away. They continued to live there normally, routinely, as if nothing had happened, whereas the Papic family, which is marked with number 9, and the Papic -- Dragan Papic's family, which has not been marked on this map and it is located right next by the road, so all these families, the Papics were at the location number 9, where this marking of X in the middle of that circle, that is where the machine-gun nest was and there was a basement there where these two families were placed. The machine-gun nest was at the corner of this house and it had like sandbags stacked up, and as far as I could notice from the distance from which I was observing, this could have been sandbags, and there was something like a machine-gun placed there, and occasionally, this weapon would be fired from, and the little forest here (indicates) between the Milicevic family home marked with 8 and the house marked with 9, so the forest between the two of them, occasionally I would see from there that it was an anti-aircraft gun or maybe submachine-gun placed on a truck, so it was a heavy piece of weapon, and occasionally this weapon would shoot at the Gornji Ahmici, upper Ahmici. The Milicevic also brought a big truck covered with a canvas canopy to their house and they unloaded something from it, I could not see what it was, it was covered by this canvas canopy, it could have been ammunition or something but I was not able to see what it was. Also in Sakib Pezer's house -- this house is at the intersection that leads up towards Ahmici from the main road -- Vlatko Kupreskic came in a vehicle, a small blue Yugo, with a couple of other people. I do not know who these other people were, but I was able to recognise him. They entered the house and next to the house was some kind of like a carpentry shop. They were bringing something out of both the house and the shop, I do not know, I could not observe what it was that they were bringing out, but they were bringing it out from both the house and the shop. On the sixth day, that is from the day of the attack, I think it was in the afternoon, a truck appeared at the intersection where I had been shot, and it came to a stop there. I was in the house and I was watching from the windows, actually still watching my parents. The truck came to collect the dead bodies. When I heard the truck arriving, I hid. There was a three-seater sofa in there, it was against a wall. I moved it, but that is where I was spending my nights, that is where I would sleep. When I would hear something, some noises, this is where I would go to hide, so that day, when I heard this truck arriving, I immediately hid behind there, and you could hear voices down there, somebody entered the house with -- talked on the radio, I could not make out what he was saying and the other one came upstairs. I think he was just checking to see whether there was something or someone upstairs, so he just peeked through the door into the room where I was and then he went back. He also checked the other rooms and then he went back downstairs. I did not see him because I was behind this sofa, I was hidden there, and after that, they collected the dead bodies and shortly thereafter, the truck left. After I was assured there were no noises any more, I came out from behind where I was hiding, and I looked and there were none of the dead bodies were there any more. I followed the truck visually from the window, and it turned off and stopped in front of my house, which is marked with number 1. It parked in front of the entrance to my house, and from the bottom floor, since it had not burned down -- we were actually preparing to open up a store there, so we had some flour and some oil and some other basic foods there. They just picked all that up and loaded it on to the truck. What I forgot to say is that whilst they had still not collected the dead bodies, my sister Melisa -- I am now going back to the first day as I lay there wounded -- I saw her on the ground next to my mother, but when I came to and I looked out of the window, I could not see my sister Melisa. She had disappeared. It was just my parents, my father, my mother and my sister Alisa. My sister Melisa was simply not there, she had simply disappeared. Her story, this is what actually happened to her, when our mother was hit, she pulled her down to the ground and she simply either fainted or went to sleep there next to her, and remained there for two days and two nights, and after those two days, she presumably -- yes, she got up and Elvir Ahmic noticed her. He and his own sister at that time were trying to leave the village, so he spotted her and he called her over to join them and to try to make it to the upper village. She refused, she told him that she was not going, that she was waiting for the mummy to wake up, because she thought that mum was asleep, she did not know that she was dead. Elvir and his sister went in the direction to the upper village, and up there he ran into the Croat soldiers, I think it was the Jokers. They stopped him and as far as I know they took him to the camp, but before they took him there, they asked him whether there was anybody alive down there. He told them about my sister, and one of them -- in fact one of them was sent down to find my sister and to bring her so that she would be taken to the camp together with Elvir and his sister. This soldier, when he came down there, when my sister heard that somebody was approaching, she lay down next to my mother and pretended to sleep. When the soldier came there, based on the description of Elvir's, the spot where my sister was, he realised that this is who it was. He called her a few times, she would not respond, then he picked her up and carried her to Elvir. When he brought her to Elvir, to the place where Elvir and his sister were waiting to be taken to the camp, the soldier who was carrying my sister approaching him and Elvir called my sister, she opened up her eyes and told the soldier to put her down, that she could walk. So my sister was taken to Elvir and they were first taken to some house in Santici and then to the camp in Dubravica, and then when I found my way out, she was released from the camp. I would like to request of your Honours that if I missed anything, if I omitted anything, that Mr. Harmon remind me of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Adnan. You are not too tired, you are all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You have stood up well, thank you. Counsel, I assume you have some questions for the witness. Go right ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Adnan, you mentioned that you saw a Croat by the name of -- an individual by the name of Vlatko Kupreskic going in and out of Pezer's shop. Was Vlatko Kupreskic a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HVO, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that you saw -- let me rephrase the question. You also mentioned, Adnan, that your father and mother had been intending to open up a shop and that there were a number of provisions inside your house and that you saw individuals going into your house and taking those provisions out. Can you describe those people who went in and out of your house and took those provisions out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in camouflage uniforms and, as far as I can recall, it was one or two men were in civilian clothes. There were five or six of them altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of provisions your father and mother had stocked for their future shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, flour, maybe about five tonnes, oil, maybe 20 cases, some sugar, salt, chocolate, candy and other provisions, house provisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers that were going in and out of your house were not UNPROFOR soldiers in camouflage uniforms, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next I would like to very quickly turn your attention to the truck and the people who were coming to collect the bodies. Did those body collectors also include Muslims as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were Muslim prisoners there who were in the camp. They were collecting the bodies, supervised by the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were ultimately rescued then, were you not, after a number of days by UNPROFOR soldiers, Adnan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I continue my story about my rescue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, very briefly describe your rescue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The eighth day, I noticed the UNPROFOR people in the village of Pirici. There were six personnel carriers, and they were making their way slowly to the village of Ahmici. There were three on the main road and three were on this byroad going up to Ahmici. That is where they came to a stop and the UNPROFOR personnel came out and were observing the village from their vehicles. I saw all this from the house, and I felt that this would be my only chance if I tried to go towards them and maybe they could help me to get out of the village, so I left the house. Since I was wounded in the leg, I staggered, always holding on to some fence or something similar, and I went until about Hidajet's house and this is down the road that leads towards the mosque. Hidajet's house, by the way, is not marked here. I came to beyond Hidajet's house to a field and the UNPROFOR was diagonally across but I could see them clearly. I decided that I would call them from there, because I was afraid to move any farther in order not to be seen by anyone. Nobody would see me from either the soldiers or anybody from the families of Papic or Milicevic, so from there I called out to the UNPROFOR people and I said, "come on, help me", in English, and then I saw them turning around, I saw them having noticed me. I lay down into the grass which was pretty high, so that nobody else would notice, spot me there. After that, when I noticed that they had spotted me, when they had heard me, I called out once more time and I continued to lie in the grass. I heard the engines running, and the first thing that crossed my mind was that the personnel carriers were leaving. I thought that maybe they think that it is some kind of a trap or something like that, and I thought that they must be leaving. However, the personnel carriers appeared between the houses, and then I could see that they were coming towards me. Three personnel carriers came over to me and the UNPROFOR personnel came out. They dressed my wounds just superficially at first and they took me into the vehicle. They did not have an interpreter with them, and I had a little bit of English. They asked me whether there were any other people around there, and they told me that they were taking me to Travnik, to the hospital. However I requested to be taken to Zenica, so we somehow communicated with words and as far as I could understand, they were telling me that they could not take me to Zenica because of some shooting, but only to Travnik. So they put me into this vehicle and I was taken to the Travnik hospital. I was in the hospital for three days and on the fourth day, I was released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One last question, Adnan. You said you saw some Muslim civilians who were detainees collecting the corpses. Could you recognise any of those Muslims? Did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not recognise anyone then, but after the war I met a guy who was one of the people collecting the dead bodies. He is from Vitez too. He was detained in a camp, he was a detainee.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have concluded my examination of Adnan Zec and I would move into evidence Prosecutor's Exhibit 141 and the attached legend and I would also move to introduce Exhibit 142 and the attached legend. Thank you, Adnan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There is no objection from the Defence, so 141 and 142, those exhibits can be introduced into evidence. Now Adnan, as the counsel for the Prosecution probably told you, this is a court of law, we have the accused here, General Blaskic, who has been accused with serious charges. It is now perfectly legitimate for his counsel to put some questions to you. Mr. Nobilo, you will be putting the questions, is that right? Cross-examined by MR. NOBILO

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you. Mr. Zec, good morning. My name is Anto Nobilo and together with my colleague Russell Hayman, I am the attorney of General Blaskic and I would like to ask a few questions in relation to what you have been telling us about. A month before the conflict, in April, you saw at the bungalow the army that came in. Is it true that you told the investigators who questioned you before that some of them wore green camouflage uniforms and others had black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure. Perhaps accidentally I got mixed up. The soldiers of the 16th April and the soldiers from October, perhaps I got mixed up and I said differently, but I am not sure at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are not sure, thank you. During your first questioning, is it true that you drew the patches that you saw then? Do you remember that, that you drew patches for the investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you draw the patches that you could recollect at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you draw a HV emblem patch then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your previous questionings, at any point did you mention HV patches that any of the soldiers had on any occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it written down in your statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw HV patches on two occasions, twice, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I saw HV patches like all the others throughout the day -- you mean HV patches at the bungalow?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How many people were there at the bungalow with HV patches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the day, as they were running by -- you said that you were lying there and they were running by, how many people did you see with HV patches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would be interested in the following: when at the cross-roads you mentioned, on the one hand there is a road going to the minaret, to the mosque, and the other road leads to upper Ahmici, you see the picture here, C, B. Tell me, these soldiers who were moving towards the mosque, how were they moving? Were they walking, were they running, were they crawling? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is as if they were hiding from someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they shooting in that direction towards the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what distance -- from what distance did you hear them? We know that you were there at the intersection and you know where the mosque was. Where were they approximately as they were shooting towards the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very close to me. Mirsad's house, Husein's house, along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by Husein's and Mirsad's house, they were there and they were shooting from there towards the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards the mosque and towards the upper part of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards the upper part of the village, yes. Can you tell me what time it was approximately? I know it was very difficult in that situation, but at least roughly what time of the day, when they were shooting towards the mosque and the upper part of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it early morning or just before noon, could you tell me that perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I had arrived, it was 5.00 or 5.30 -- I cannot really orient myself, it is difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell me how many people were involved in the fighting towards the mosque, how many people did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The army, these men were coming and going. They were going up there towards Zijad's house too. As far as I can remember, I already mentioned that that day, I saw over 100 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 100 people were coming and going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these the same people or different people? You do not know actually how many people you saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At any rate, not less than 100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you include in these 100 the people who were coming back? Do you know that the same people would come and go by you several times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, the neighbours, Croats, men, did they wear uniforms before the conflict, most of them, or all of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Dragan Papic, I can say that throughout the period from October to April wore black uniform all the time. I do not know if I ever saw him without a black uniform and he also had a flag on his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not have to tell me about every one of them now. The younger Croats, did they wear uniforms before the fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Younger Croats, I am not sure, but one of the Milicevics, I think he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These neighbours of yours, did they go to the front-line or were they only there in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you give the investigators a note about who is responsible for the killings in Nadioci, a note that you wrote in accordance to what your aunt told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to read it to you now and tell me is that that note: "Miroslav Bralo, called Cicko, from the village of Nadioci said, 'yesterday in Ahmici I slaughtered and killed everyone and torched everything and now you are next'. Then he took out a bloody knife and he said, 'now you are next'. He was referring to the civilians who are kept in a house above Nadioci from the village of Loncari. Miroslav Bralo, Cicko, also said that he killed 17 Muslims from Nadioci on a tractor on which they were moving towards Muslim territory."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain to us how this note was written and is it true, or rather did I read correctly what you wrote then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you read it properly. It is the story of my aunt, who was a prisoner there in that house, and who heard this conversation, or rather what he was saying, and it related to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you wrote it down then so that you would not forget it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know anything about the establishment of checkpoints in the village of Ahmici, in October, within the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain it to us in a couple of sentences what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a checkpoint below my house, so my house is number 1, so this is a curve below my house (indicates). It was a checkpoint to prevent the Croat army from passing towards Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who established the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did it consist of, this checkpoint, this roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A few hedgehogs and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. Can I ask or can I explain the reason for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Questioning about checkpoints was not gone into on direct examination. He merely recounted the story of the massacre of his family and his survival, so I would object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained. I was about to myself in respect of the note which had not been addressed in the course of examination, so please, Mr. Nobilo, move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I certainly accept that the cross-examination has to relate to the examination-in-chief, so we are going to conclude our questioning now and we are going to reserve the right to perhaps call this witness during our part of the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will see about that in due time, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I think my colleague's point, your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, go right ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It might be efficient if Mr. Nobilo has a couple of questions which are beyond the scope and perhaps the Prosecution would even agree to do that now, rather than have him come all the way back in our case. We simply raise that possibility. We do not wish to inconvenience the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hayman. To tell you the truth, the court would be quite reluctant to have the witness return in a few weeks or a few months time, I can tell you that right now. The court had decided on something quite clear-cut, that is to say the cross-examination had to be suited, adjusted to the examination-in-chief. Now this goes for you today, but the same will apply when you are making your case. I will say the same thing to the Prosecution. That is the rule, I do not know if we can call it a rule, in a very flexible manner, I did not interrupt you, for instance, when Mr. Nobilo asked the question about the note that had been submitted to the investigators, I was waiting for an objection on the part of the Prosecution in fact, because there is going to be these questions and we have already dwelled on a sufficient number of painful matters. Now let me see, do you want to ask some additional questions, redirect, react to the questions from the Defence, Mr. Harmon? Re-examined by MR. HARMON

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Adnan, you mentioned in one of your answers to Mr. Nobilo that Dragan Papic hung a flag out of his house. What kind of a flag was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, it is the flag of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just -- fellow judges, Judge Riad? So we are going to proceed to a recess, that way the witness will also be able to rest a bit, and we are going to resume at 2.45 this afternoon. (12.25 pm) (Adjourned until 2.45 pm) 23 24 25 (2.45 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The court is back in session. Please bring in the accused, Mr. Registrar. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So we are going to resume. Adnan, did you have lunch, you have rested up a bit? How do you feel, do you feel okay? Good. We have just about done, but the judges would like to put some additional questions to you. I am going to immediately cede the floor to Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Adnan. You have been sadly present in these very unhappy events where you lost your family. I believe your direct experience can help us visualise the global picture of your first-hand knowledge. I would like to start with the beginning of your testimony. You mentioned that before the events, which was 15th April, the Croatian children did not attend school, and at another phase of your testimony, you mentioned that Croats like Papic and Milicevic left their homes and came back several days later. That was before the events happened? When the children did not come to school, everything was still quiet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they took their families towards the dusk on April 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there was no shooting then or anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the media announce that there would be shooting or anything, or they did it quietly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, nobody knew anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except they seemed to have known, I mean otherwise they would not have left, there was some kind of agreement among them to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some kind of planning, let us say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that way. That is, among the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the Croats. When we come to the killing phase, I want first to know, when your father was killed, was he -- did he have any weapon on him, was he fighting back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your mother shot at or was she killed by accident and your sister, I think your sister Alisa, were they executed or just shot at because there was shooting everywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is impossible that they were shot accidentally, and if it is necessary, I can clarify further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not need that, I just want to know. So people were shot even without fighting or without carrying weapons, men as well as women, as well as children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And without any discrimination, anybody would be shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were walkie-talkies and there were radio transmitters, you heard orders given from soldiers to other soldiers to execute orders; you heard, for instance, that on the transmitter they were asking for explosives to lower Ahmici. Was there any attack to lower Ahmici; why did they need the explosives for lower Ahmici? Was there anybody attacking from lower Ahmici? Did they need to defend anything? What were the explosives for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked for the explosives for the lower mosque in Ahmici. As I said before, they attacked us and we were unarmed, we completely did not expect any kind of attack. For instance the case of my own family, we were all at home asleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said there were 100 soldiers shooting towards upper Ahmici with machine-guns placed on a truck. Was there anybody shooting back? Were these 100 soldiers attacked to shoot back or what was it, was it a battle or were they shooting to destroy something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe that there was any battle, any fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all the events you saw, the man killed your parents, and the other people you saw from where you were living, and the others you noticed, did you have the impression that there were unrelated groups, each group doing what he wants, or was it an organised team acting with co-ordination and according to hierarchy and orders? Do you understand me? Was it just something which lacked organisation, anarchy, you know, or a team, well organised, of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I could see, my inference is that this was a very well planned and well organised operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And orders would be obeyed and given from one to other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nobody would do what he likes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Adnan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Riad. Judge Shahabuddeen, will you also be putting questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Adnan Zec, I have two small questions for you, and they probably are not terribly important either. The first one is this: you went to school on the 15th April; where was that school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second question is this: after you were shot and you managed eventually to get up, you entered a building and you remained there for some time. I think the building was at point 6 on the diagram. Could you refresh me by telling me how long you stayed in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
