utterances.text: About seven days. Also that means I was outside for one day, and I was inside seven days, so eight days in total before I came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is this: during that time, did you find anything to eat or to drink?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had water, so I only drank water and I found a little bit of jam, like marmalade, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we are done, Adnan Zec. You have stood up very well indeed, this evoked a lot of suffering for you and the Tribunal would like to thank you again and wishes you the best in future, that you recover your peace of mind. I am not going to ask you what you are doing now because we do not want to identify you, but you are a young man and we do hope you will be making the most of your life in future. Mr. Registrar, perhaps we could lower the blinds so that the witness might leave the courtroom without being seen from the public gallery. We do want to enforce the protective measures as best we can. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you are going to be speaking on behalf of the Prosecution. We are listening to you. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you. Good afternoon, your Honours. The next witness is a woman by the name of Djula Dzidic. As with the other witness, the only protective measure that Ms Dzidic requests is a facial distortion, no body distortion, so she is not viewed on television. I have discussed this with Mr. Nobilo prior to commencement of this afternoon's session. With regard to the evidence to be offered by Ms Dzidic, and I will say, your Honour, we will be quite brief with this witness, we will not go through repetition on this witness, she does offer us another view within several areas of Zume, which is part of Santici, where camouflage and black-clad soldiers were operating together in unison. In addition, she will offer us evidence on the direct killings by these soldiers of Ismail Ahmic, Mujo Ahmic and Fadil Pezer. She will then recount exactly what happened to her thereafter at the hands of other HVO soldiers, again dressed in camouflage, being moved to an HVO location near the Pican cafe and then the taking of her, along with approximately 50 other women and children, to the Dubravica school, walking in a column, taking them to Dubravica school. I will say this, Mr. President, consistent with your instructions, we have photographs of her brothers who were killed that day, never seen again, and with the court's permission I will introduce those, because I do not really think that she will make it through that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: She has agreed to being shown those photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but I will tell, consistent with Mr. President, your instructions, I will describe what the photographs are so she does not have to, because I think she will get very upset about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. I think that is the right way to do it. Now we are going to proceed as we did this morning. I was grateful to Mr. Harmon for having gone ahead in that way, I think it is efficient and I think Mr. Harmon did ask any questions he had, so I do think it is a good idea to let the witness -- for witnesses to be allowed to express themselves freely and then you put the questions which you think are particularly relevant for the case of the Prosecution. Now Mr. Registrar, if you could have Ms. Dzidic brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could also ask the Registrar to pull out Exhibit 120. We have two previously marked exhibits and then 120, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Now you are going first of all to simply tell me your first and last name, since that can be disclosed, just your first and last name. Ms.?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Djula Dzidic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if you would please read out the solemn declaration. Please remain seated when you do so. We are listening to you. MS. DJULA DZIDIC (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Now you have received protective measures, the Defence has gone along with that, the court has accepted it as well, so you can speak freely before the judges who, of course, are going to be giving you their full attention. There will be a few, short bit of questions relating to identification, then you will testify quite freely, in your own words, about the essential aspects. You do not need to be too lengthy, needless to say, and thereafter the counsel for the Prosecution will put the questions to you relevant to the case against General Blaskic. After that, the Defence will be putting questions to you and then thereafter the judges as well. If you do feel tired, do not be shy, simply let me know and we will take the appropriate measures so you have a chance to have a rest. There you are, counsel for the Prosecution, proceed, please. Examined by MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djula, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am 38 now and I was 33 then, so I would 38 by the end of this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djula, on 16th April 1993, did you live in Zume with your parents and your brothers and your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I lived with my mother and my brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had your family lived in Zume?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 21 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where had they moved from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We moved from the village of Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zume is a part of Santici, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zume a relatively new village being started in approximately 1970, 1971?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there both Muslims and Croats living in Zume and Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djula, you and your family are Muslims, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to 16th April 1993, Djula, and in your own words, tell the judges what happened to you and your family on 16th April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will start on that morning. We did not know anything. In the morning, it was about 5.15 on Friday, the first explosion we heard was coming from the neighbour's house, that is what woke us up. We got up and in the meantime, a lot of bullets were fired into the house, the windows and elsewhere, we could not get out. First my mother and I were there, my oldest brother lived in the summer kitchen with his wife and two children, so my mother came out first, then I did, so that we would not be there. We crossed over to Mehmed Ahmic's house, and went into his basement and after about 15 minutes I happened to go upstairs and saw that our house was being torched. I saw two neighbours who were going down the road and they turned off and came to my house. They belonged to the HVO. One of them called me out and I came down. I heard the shooting meanwhile, and when I approached, there was a dead body there and next to the house, there were two other dead bodies. They were lying on their stomachs. I asked where to go next. He first asked me who else was in the house, and I told him there was a woman with two children and some elderly women and Mehmed Ahmic and his wife. I said, "where are we to go?", and he said, "to Vitez". So we started, we went along the road and we arrived at Pican's cafe. There Zilic came over, and he was in civilian clothes with a rifle, and we said, "where now?", and he said, "to Dedic's garage", and we were locked up there until 5.00. Around 5.00, we went to Nesib Ahmic's house, but there was another family of Hrjnic, the whole family was brought there, husband, wife and two sons, and they brought him and his youngest brother and wife and they were locked up and we heard a shot and Mehmed Hrjnic, his other son was lying on the floor. Then we went to Nesib Ahmic's house. There we spent the whole night, nobody was guarding us. In the morning, they took us to a shop, which was above Pican's house, and that day we spent there. Sunday morning, we were taken to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to be asked questions, I would prefer to be asked some questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask a few questions about what happened on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please. Yes please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the Registrar, if I could give the witness what has been previously marked as 143A, which is a map, and there is a legend attached to that which is 143B. If I could ask the usher if we could put this on the ELMO? Djula, you see the map that is before you with the circles, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You assisted us in identifying the locations that are circled, the houses that are circled, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your house is number 1, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that your oldest brother lived with his family in the summer kitchen behind you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 2 is Mehmed Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to the second floor of Mehmed Ahmic's house, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the second floor of Mehmed Ahmic's house, did you see any HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were holding Pezer -- Mujo Ahmic and -- yes, you could see everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many HVO soldiers did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came downstairs, I saw a total of five. When they called me out, when I came over to my house, I saw a total of five of them. One was there when he was calling me out, because they spotted me upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were these soldiers dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in camouflage and black camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these soldiers that were dressed in camouflage and black, did they seem to you to be working together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you were looking down at the second floor, you said that these soldiers had Ismail Ahmic, Mujo Ahmic and Fadil Pezer in custody, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said that one of those HVO soldiers called you downstairs, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your way downstairs, did you hear any gun shots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, while I was coming down the stairs, I heard shots and when I was coming out of the house of Mehmed Ahmic, I heard the shots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got back downstairs, where were Ismail Ahmic, Mujo Ahmic and Fadil Pezer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ismail Ahmic was in front of my house and Fadil Pezer and Mujo Ahmic were at the corner of my house, up from the staircase. They were lying down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they bleeding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were lying in front of your house, which is marked on the map as number 1, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they appear to you to be dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These soldiers that you said were in camouflage and black uniforms, did they have any coloured arm bands on their epaulettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any hand-held radios?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of radios did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Black, it was black. Small like this (indicates) and black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told the judges that you saw from Mehmed Ahmic's house that your house was being set on fire, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the judges what you saw about how your house was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them taking the gasoline and pouring it and then setting it on fire. They had big canisters and they started from the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they had socks on their faces, I could not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to your house being set on fire, were other houses around your house also being set on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were all on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this group of soldiers moving from house to house to set them on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately when I was coming over to ask where to go next, they just moved straight on to the next house, and setting it afire, because they knew that the house was empty. The moment we came out of Mehmed Ahmic's house and were told to go to Vitez, that is what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djula, let me turn your attention back to the house on the ELMO. You identified your house as number 1 and Mehmed Ahmic's house as number 2. Whose house is number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ismail Ahmic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was one of the men that was murdered in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Because they were going along the side of the road, and they brought them to our house, so the soldiers brought them over there so that my family would come out too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 4 on the map, whose house is that? Is that Fadil Pezer's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He is another man that was murdered by HVO soldiers in front of number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 5 is whose house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of Sefik Pezer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sefik Pezer is the father of Fadil Pezer, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Ibro is his father, Ibro Pezer. Also he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All these houses that you saw burning, as well as the men that you saw murdered in front of your house, were all the houses owned by Muslims and were all the men that you saw murdered Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were told by one of these soldiers to go towards Pican's cafe. Is that designated on the map as number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers around Pican's cafe when you went down there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the cafe and one of them was outside, but he was wearing civilian clothes, this Zilo Zilic, and I asked him, "where shall we go?", because I thought he was a civilian, and he told us to go to the Dedic garage, but as we were going along the road, no, I did not see anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were leaving the area from Ahmic Mehmed's house, who went with you from Mehmed Ahmic's house to the Pican cafe. Who went with you, without identifying; was it your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Members of my family, and Mehmed Ahmic and his wife and no one else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your two brothers with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had happened to your two brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw my brothers when they tried to get away to Pirici. They crossed the fence and I never saw them again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continuing on, you were told when you got to Pican's cafe, you were told to then go to Mujo Dedic's garage, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you moved to Mujo Dedic's garage, which is designated on the map as number 7, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see more soldiers moving from house to house in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I just saw these civilians as we were going towards the garage. We found this family in the garage already. I did not see anyone else, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers around there at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only when we got out of the garage and that was 5.00 in the evening. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the garage, the Hrjnic family went into the garage with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they came afterwards. We were there and they brought them three hours after us. They brought them subsequently, three hours after us, the army brought them or someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then, after they brought the Hrjnics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were putting people gradually into the garage, one by one, and then they were locking and unlocking the garage, so they brought his wife and his younger son and the husband and the older son remained. We heard shooting, you could see it too, because they shot them in the back with automatic rifles, because there was a big hole in the garage door. So we could see, but we do not know who they were, no. And they let us out of the garage already around 5.00, they locked the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the shooting was going on, were there soldiers outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only saw two of them while they were lining these people up to shoot them. I heard them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were dressed the same way, they wore the same uniforms, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour were these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you stayed in that garage for a period of time until about 5.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then go to Nesib Ahmic's house, which is designated on the map as number 8?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a weekend cottage, the downstairs part had been burned down, the upstairs not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you went into Nesib Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got into the cottage and we spent the night there, upstairs. We were on our own, no one guarded us, we could not go anywhere. But in the morning, at 7.30, on Saturday, being civilians, we were taken to the building where the shop was. Again, near Pican's cafe, we took the same road. This was Saturday morning already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the morning of the 17th, Saturday morning, did someone come to Nesib Ahmic's house to talk to you, did a Bosnian Croat come to that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, our neighbour Vrebac came, he was not armed or anything, it was as if he wanted to help us. We said we wanted to go to Sivrino Selo and he said we could not and then he took us to another house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Vrebac family lives in the four sided roof house that is on the map as number 9, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Vrebac family are Croats, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you asked Vrebac to go to Sivrino Selo, did he tell you why you could not go to Sivrino Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were not allowed to go because we would be killed by the HVO, by their people. It was not safe for us. They would not let us, so it was not safe to go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Djula, who told you that if you went to Sivrino Selo you would be killed by the HVO? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The man who brought us from that house, Vrebac, the one who took us to the shop. We asked him, we did not have anyone else to ask, so we asked him and he told us that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you went to a location that was marked on the map as number 10, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened at that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got in there, we did not know that we will be spending the entire night there. In the meantime, various groups arrived, so we were all brought there together, there were over 50 of us, women and children, young people, some young people up to the ages of 13 or 14. Later on, they also brought in Ahmic Zenur, four young men altogether. There were there for half an hour, they rested up a bit and after that, a HVO soldier came and said they could go, as if they were supposed to collect dead bodies, but these people never came back, I never saw them again, so that is where we spent the entire night. Anto Papic guarded us that night, and in the morning the Croat women who lived nearby in the houses wanted to bring us something to help us, and finally we did not want anything. On Sunday morning at 7.30 again we were taken to the camp by Nikica, to the school. That is at the railway station, four kilometres away from us in Dubravica. All the women and children were all there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that men were taken out to dig trenches. Who took the men out to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we were put into the different class rooms, women and children were in the class rooms, there were men who were brought in from Vitez and we actually found them there when we arrived. They were taken away to dig trenches. This happened on Sunday, so various incidents occurred. They would come back late in the evening. It was simply terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me backtrack a second, I got ahead of myself. You said that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that four men were taken out to pick up bodies. Did an HVO soldier take those men out to pick up bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was that soldier dressed, or soldiers dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see if he had any insignias on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not pay attention. Fear. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the location number 10, the HVO headquarters in Santici, did you see UNPROFOR in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in the afternoon, Saturday afternoon, around 4.00 I think. They were coming and it was not that I was the only woman, there were many women, so this Ivica Vidovic, called Jevdjo, worked with them and we asked for help to be taken away but he would not let us come and talk to them at all, so I did not talk to them at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question about that. You said you wanted to talk to UNPROFOR. Who would not let you talk to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivica Vidovic, Jevdjo, he would not let us talk to them, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Jevdjo, Ivica Vidovic, was he a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So neither you nor any other women or children, or anyone located at number 10, was permitted to talk to UNPROFOR, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you ultimately were taken to the school at Dubravica, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people that were in this house were taken to the school at Dubravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some children, some women, 50 of us altogether. But as far as the garage is concerned, there were 30 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were 30 in the garage and then there were 50 brought down to the Dubravica school, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and afterwards more people were brought in, on Saturday more people were brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get from the house in Santici to the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On foot, along the road. A HVO soldier took us, Nikica Plavcic. He is the only one who went with us to Dubravica. We walked on foot all the way along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you walk in a column down the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Column, in a column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were 50, approximately 50, mostly women and children, walking down the road with an HVO soldier guarding you, down to the Dubravica school, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, just one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivica Plavcic was a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the Dubravica school, were there soldiers at the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we found soldiers at the school and they took us over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what type of soldiers were at the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not know them at all, we only knew Marinko, because he was responsible. This Plavcic Marinko, he was the only one who was responsible for us, but not for others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any members of the Vitezovi at the Dubravica school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all had insignia and black uniforms. Most of them had black uniforms, as far as we are concerned, I mean the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn that some of them were members of the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that, yes. That is some kind of special unit of theirs, but I could not tell, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can, with the assistance of the usher, if we could place Exhibit 120 on the ELMO? This is a photograph that has previously been received in evidence, Mr. President. Djula, I have shown you this photograph before, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your house in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not A, the building in front of me, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about over to the right, the one marked C?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could then put 143A back on the ELMO. Djula, you said that on the morning of the 16th, your two brothers Nedzad and Muharem left the house when the shooting started and you never saw them again. Did you learn that they had been seen at the location number 11 on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After we were exchanged by the Red Cross, I sought the truth and the only thing I was told was that they arrived there alive and that is all I know, and that is the way it is until the present day. I also know because of their clothes. My younger brother had a sports suit and the other one just had -- my older brother had trousers and a shirt and they both had shoes and that is the only thing I remembered, nothing else until the present day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw your brothers that morning, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have uniforms on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old were your brothers on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, I know that my older brother was born on 25th May 1965 and my youngest brother was born on 8th January 1972, but now this very moment I cannot think of it, so my younger brother was 21 then, I think, and the older one was about 30, not more than 30. I mean in 1963, so in 1993 ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you never saw your brothers after 16th April 1993. Did you or any family member recover their bodies after that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never. I investigated and I wanted to get their bodies, but no. We tried to identify them by their clothes, because we got a list of the dead bodies that were found, and that is how I came to this conclusion, but no, we never found the bodies themselves, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as discussed previously, the witness has given the Office of the Prosecutor two photographs, marked at this point as 144/1, which is her brother Nedzad, and 144/2, which is her brother Muharem. We would offer those into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No objection from the Defence with regard to introducing those to the case file?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could we see them? (Handed). No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So we have introduced these as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Lastly, Mr. President, the location that is marked number 11 was a house that was being built by a woman by the name of Senada, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would offer into evidence 143A, which is the map, and 143B, which is the legend attached to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is fine, so we will enter those into evidence. You have done, have you, counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, you are now going to be questioned, as the Office of the Prosecutor will no doubt have told you, by the counsel for General Blaskic. It is Mr. Nobilo who is going to be putting the questions to you. Please proceed, counsel. Cross-examined by MR. NOBILO

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Miss Dzidic, as you have heard I am Anto Nobilo, the attorney of General Blaskic, and Mr. Russell Hayman is also General Blaskic's attorney. On behalf of the Defence only one or two questions. Your brothers, Muharem and Nedzad, were they members of the TO or the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brothers, no. My brother worked and the other one, no. My older brother worked at the Impregnacija, at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they members of the TO or the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When one of your brothers was getting dressed, did he take part of a military uniform, did he ask you for part of a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he just asked for clothes. He asked for a vest, but not a military vest. I know what I am saying. This is a vest that I could wear or anybody could wear, you know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor that Nedzad asked you to give him his military vest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Additional questions from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So my dear colleagues, do you have questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Djula Dzidic. I just wanted to know, when you were in the school of Dubravica, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the 18th until the 22nd -- from the 18th until the 1st of May and we were registered on the 22nd when the Red Cross came. The 18th in the morning until 1st May. We only got out on 1st May and the Red Cross came on 22nd and they registered us all. They brought us food and they also made it possible for us to wash, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the treatment in this camp? Was it a concentration camp? What was it like exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For us it was terrible, but these were classrooms. It is a school, you know, with classrooms, so there was a hallway too and we were staying in the classrooms, that is where we had beds also, they allowed us to have beds, and that is where we stayed. But the camp, no, it is like a school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not like a prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looked like a prison, but it is not a real prison, not a real prison, because it is a school. We were not allowed to go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why were you taken there in the first place? Why did they take you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Believe me, I have no idea. We were waiting for this exchange, because allegedly we were supposed to be exchanged and they did not have any place to put us. So their army was there and that is why we were there. They did not know what to do with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your house has been put on fire, you said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who put it on fire? Were they soldiers or people from the area? Who was putting the houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were wearing military uniforms, naturally they were soldiers, but who they were, I could not recognise them. They were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Miss Dzidic, you spoke about Pican's cafe and you told us about a man whose name I think was Zilo Dzidic, and you thought he was a civilian, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Zilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am at fault. Did you know Mr. Zilic before that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is one of the locals, he also had a shop there, a butcher's shop, and he built a house there and that is where -- there was a bus stop where I caught my bus when I went to work to Travnik, I grew up there and I knew practically everyone. He was a neighbour, he was wearing civilian clothes, so I asked him to help us, but he held a gun in his hands. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you knew him, did he always wear civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of your neighbours also members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, your memory goes back to a time before the HVO was formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Practically all that started in 1992, from 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also saw the development of the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know that that was their name, it was all the same to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the first time you saw the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the conflict, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Your testimony is now over. The Tribunal would like to thank you very much for coming to testify here from so far away and we do hope that you find peace of mind in future. Do not move for the time being, we are going to see to the appropriate protective measures, so we are going to let the blinds down so that no one outside the courtroom can see your face. There you are, I think that now you may rise. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Now it is Ms Paterson. Good afternoon. You are going to introduce the next witness? I assume that we are keeping these protective measures up? It is a protected witness we are talking about, and I suppose you have talked to the Defence about it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, this witness has requested the same protection as the previous two witnesses today. She just wants her face covered from the television cameras and she is willing to allow us to use her name. I informed Mr. Nobilo of this before the court session this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Before the witness comes into the room, could you briefly tell us what your expectations are in connection with the Prosecution's case against General Blaskic? What is the witness going to be testifying about? Who is the witness, first of all? Is it a gentleman, a lady?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, this witness's name is Azra Dedic. Her testimony in many ways will complement that of the witness who has just finished. In fact, it was the garage which belonged to Ms. Dedic's family where the previous witness and Ms. Dedic were detained for a period of time on 16th April 1993. Ms. Dedic will describe what happened to her family and several of her close neighbours on that day. She will be able to describe sightings of a significant number of HVO soldiers in the area. She will unfortunately describe the death of her husband and son and several of her neighbours and she will describe some of the same incidents that followed that this witness has just talked about, I think she can give complementary testimony, I do not think it will really be repetitive. As with the previous witness, I have a diagram I will show her. She brought some family photographs and the agreement I have with her concerning the photographs is I will ask her at the time if she wants to be shown the photographs. If she feels she is up to it, I will show them to her; if not, I am prepared to introduce them just as Mr. Kehoe did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, thank you very much. Now Mr. Registrar, we can have Ms. Azra Dedic come in. How long do you plan for her testimony to last, Ms Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: I think it will be approximately the same length as the previous witness, no longer. Approximately an hour, no more than an hour and a half. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me, madam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, thank you for having come. First please tell us your first and last names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Azra Dedic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, please remain seated and read the declaration which the person next to you is going to provide you with. MS. AZRA DEDIC (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Ms Paterson is going to put a few questions to you and then you are going to talk about the events you witnessed in your own words, in the manner you see fit. In all likelihood thereafter the counsel for the Prosecution will be putting some questions to you in connection with the case against General Blaskic. He has been accused and he has counsel, and counsel for the Defence, of course, will be putting questions to you as well. Now, we could have some preliminary questions and then we will listen to the narrative from Ms. Azra Dedic. Examined by MS. PATERSON

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Ms. Dedic, were you living in the village of Santici in Bosnia-Herzegovina in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you lived in that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 24 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell the court who you were living with at your home in April 1993, what family members lived with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived with my husband and two sons that I had. Then the older son, when he got married, he moved to a new house and that is where he lived for seven months with his wife and small baby Ilma, who is six months old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell the court the names of your husband and your two sons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband's name was Mustafa Dedic, the older son was Fariz Dedic and the youngest, Haris Dedic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your husband, was he known by a nickname or a shortened version of his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His name was Mustafa, but they called him -- we all called him Mujo. Everybody called him that, all neighbours and everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell the court the age of your two sons in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son Fariz was three days short of being 23, and the youngest son was -- they were six and a half years apart so I would have to calculate, you see. So 23 and there is -- the younger one was not adult yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you and the members of your family Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the months preceding April 1993, were either your husband or either of your sons in the Territorial Defence or in the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son Fariz was in the Territorial Defence and my husband worked in the Sumarija in Vitez, so he had work duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in other words, instead of working for the TO or the military, your husband was required to go to his regular job every day, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, I am going to ask you to tell the court what happened to you and your family on 16th April, but before you begin I would like to ask the usher to show you an exhibit which I believe has been premarked number 145. This is an aerial photograph. Could you please show it to the witness and put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the main road leading to Vitez and Sarajevo. We lived, looking from Vitez, to the right-hand side and looking from Busovaca to the left-hand side, so our houses were on the right-hand side, looking from Vitez. I will start from D, that is my sister's house, Semra Ribo. D is my son Fariz's house, and A is my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, let me just interrupt for a moment. Your son's house, is that B or D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And my house is A, and E is the garage in front of my house and C is Islam Ahmic's house, and D is Sefik Ahmic's house, that is the brother of Islam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, let me just interrupt again. Is D the house of your sister or the house of Sefik Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: D is my sister's. Number 2 is Sefik Ahmic's house. It is only now that I saw it properly, so I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That morning, 16th April, because my husband had this work duty, like every day he went to catch the bus to go first to Rijeka, not directly to Vitez, and the bus was leaving 5.15, 5.30 and it had already started, he was halfway down the hallway, I was following him, and we heard the powerful explosion and he said, "Azra, it is over, wake up Haris and let us move over to Fariz's place". I went to the bedroom and I rose Haris and I told him we were all going to Fariz's place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, can I just interrupt for a moment. I know you are a little bit nervous. You are speaking very fast; can you just slow down a little bit so the interpreters can get everything you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I will. As I was going, that is crossing from my house to my son's house, I lost the sight of my husband, and as I was crossed over, I saw Islam Ahmic on his balcony and he said, "where is Mustafa?", and I said, "he went into Fariz's house". He said, "they are shooting, I have been hit, go back into the house", and, of course, I went into the house, that is my son's house, and my son Haris followed me. When we were inside, my husband was peeking occasionally through the window, looking towards the main road. At one point, he said, "there is a woman coming, I do not know who it is, Azra". At that moment, he was still peeking a little bit and he said, "they are shooting", and the shooting was coming from all sides and he told me and my little granddaughter and my daughter-in-law to go into a pit, it was like a staircase, and Hadisa Pezer arrived, she was a younger woman and my husband probably did not know her, and as she walked in, she said, "there is shooting everywhere, do not go out. I am coming from down below, from the Pezer's house. All our houses are on fire and all our men have been killed". Then she went down into this little basement with us, and the shooting continued from everywhere. She sat down by the door and Fariz said, "are they looking for weapons?", and she said, "they are". He had a pistol, he was a forester so he got it from his company. He showed it to her and she said, "whether you had it or not, they will shoot you". At that point, somebody says, "who is at home?". My husband came out and I followed him. There was a dark young man in a camouflage uniform, no mask or anything. He had a gun in his hand and my husband, who was beside himself, said, "what is going on? What do you think you are doing?". He said, "what about what happened in Zenica?". He said, "I do not know, I am just doing my job". At that moment, I had a good view from my sister's house, I could see a column of soldiers coming and they were already approaching. This same soldier, I had a good view, about 30 metres ahead of me, and as I was standing next to my husband, he looked under and he said, "madam, what is down there?"; I said, "garage". "Can you unlock it for me?"; "I would have to go over to my house because that is where the keys are"; "if you do not mind, go over there". I went over there and unlocked it while my husband was talking to this young man, I do not know what he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please try and speak a little bit more slowly, I know you are nervous, but it is important the court hear your story and hear it correctly. Try and speak as slowly as you can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I went and unlocked the garage, I came back over there, in front of my son's house and my son had already taken -- but as I was coming back from the garage, I crossed over into my house and I saw my son as he was taking the baby in the cradle to his wife and I stayed in the house. I was thinking a little bit about maybe they should have taken some clothes, I do not know what, it was 10 or 15 minutes past and I heard my son Haris's voice, "mum, mum, come out because they will kill you". Then I came out and there were other people coming to my yard. I saw Mehmed and there were some others below the garage who were arriving, so I saw some people in the garage and I saw other people arriving, but I was the last one to go into the garage and I barely had room to fit in there. My husband stayed in front of the house, in front of my son's house. He was still talking to this young man. At that moment, as I was coming inside the garage, I already saw that there were a lot of soldiers in Islam's yard, and I saw them coming, even more of them. Islam's children were there, Islam was there, near that pillar, and a soldier was walking around as if he was guarding us a little bit, but he was also putting us in this garage. As we all packed into this garage, this one soldier yelled over to the other one, "lock it up and if anybody comes out, shoot". So we stayed there locked in the garage. I do not know how much it could have been, one or five minutes, we heard bursts of fire. After that, a dead silence fell for about ten minutes, fifteen. Then we heard a voice, and since I could not see, we could not see from this garage, we could only see straight out to the main road, Hrjnic, Meho Hrjnic was coming and Ado Hrjnic and behind them was his wife and his son Haris. We could see them as they were coming because we had a clear view from the garage on to the main road, and behind them, behind the four of them there were two soldiers. As they came halfway towards the house of my son, somebody must have said to Meho to stay there and he did. There was a soldier next to him. The other soldier escorted Ado and Haris and Samija. When they came, the door was unlocked and they entered, Samija and Haris, and Ado stepped in -- Admir was his name, Ado was his nickname. The soldier behind him told him, "hey, you, come back too", and he did go back to that road by the main road, because his father was still standing there, not quite on the road, but a step away from the road. It was just like a little -- there was like -- turned a little bit towards Fariz's house. Ado also arrived there and stood next to his father and the two soldiers who were there, they shot him in, I do not know, the back or stomach, I do not know, and they fell down. They tried to go forward and then a minute later, their hair just sort of stood up. There was then some panic, some silence, there were about 30 of us in this garage, and this went on until about 3.35 or 4.00. We did not have watches, it was just women and children. Then down the same road, there were three neighbours of ours, I knew them well. One's name was Srebrenica, I do not know his first name. The other one was Draze, I know that one well, and Zoran maybe, a blond one. Whether they had uniforms or not, I really did not remember that, but they went -- were walking and they looked out, Meho and Ado are lying, they came in front of my house, where I lived, they drank some water, they stood there, maybe they had a bottle of something, I do not know, some kind of beverage, I do not know what it was, and we yelled from the garage, Djula Dzidic she knew them a bit better, she was also with us, and we called them, called them, "Zoran, Zoran, open up" and they came over and unlocked us. We all came out into the yard and some people drank some water. If they had anything in their bags, they also had something to eat, and I quickly went to the barn so that I could milk the cow because I had the granddaughter, so I want wanted to bring her some milk. We asked them, "where should we go, what should we do?". One of them crossed the yard and went into my other sister's house. He said, "you know, it is not safe here". The first floor was on fire and it burnt down, but the top floor remained intact and we were going to go there and he said, "it is not safe there, but Nesib Ahmic, he has a summer kitchen", so we moved over there, we went up --

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, let me stop you at this point in time. If it is all right with Mr. President, I would like to go back and ask some questions at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps we could take a break now, everyone could rest up, the interpreters, the witness, unless you have a short question, otherwise we will have the recess now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I think this is a perfect time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. We will resume then at 4.35. (4.15 pm) (A short break) (4.35 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The court is back in session. Bring in the accused, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, at this point in time I am just going to ask you a few questions to clarify some parts of the story you just told the judges. You said when you came out of your house to go next door to your son Fariz's house, you had a short conversation with Islam Ahmic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me -- actually he and I were the only ones facing each other, and he kept saying, "where is Mujo?" -- "where is Mustafa?", I mean, and I said, "he got into the house, Harisa's house", and he was on a terrace and he said at that point, "Azra, get into the house quickly, you too, I have already been hit". I saw him from that terrace making this kind of sign (indicates) and then he left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you actually see Islam Ahmic shot and killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see when he was hit. He just managed to tell me this when he was getting back into the house. I was downstairs and he was on a terrace. I was already in front of my son's house, and he asked me, "where is Mujo?", and I said, "he got in here", and that is what he managed to tell me. He said, "I have been hit too, get into the house quickly", and he went into his house and I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed later that Islam Ahmic in fact had been killed by that shot and died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as we were getting out of the house again, when I was coming back to the garage when my son called me, when I was getting out of my house a minute or two later, Islam Ahmic was standing on the ground. He, Majda and both sons, Amil and Miza, they were standing out there and next to them, I saw a soldier standing next to them. I also went on to the garage and then his sons and his wife also came into the garage with us, and Islam remained standing there by that post. I saw him standing on his own feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You also said that at some point in time when you had come out of your house, you saw a number of soldiers in the field nearby. Do you recall how many soldiers you saw in the field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I was not counting them, but a line of them were standing up there, they were walking up to us and some of them had already reached Islam's yard and they were doing something in the yard and one of them was standing and talking to my husband, my husband was still there and the man he was talking to was still there. How many of them were there, I do not know, but they were coming in and some of them had already arrived. I do not know exactly how many of them were there in the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw the troops in the field, can you estimate? Was it as few, for example, as five, or as many as 50, or do you simply have no idea how many it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, most probably I saw some ten-odd people, because that is how much I could see in front of me, about ten or twenty, something like that. As many as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, I would like to direct your attention back to the enlarged aerial photo which is exhibit number 145. Do you see a number of Xs on that photo above the large circle? Do those Xs represent the place where you saw these soldiers in the field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them roughly there, yes, as they were coming -- they were coming from that direction, yes, from up there. By my sister's house, and behind Islam's garage from that side. As they were approaching my house, at that point in time I saw Sefik's house on fire -- Sefik was Islam's brother -- so they were coming from that side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see whether or not these soldiers were wearing uniforms and if so, could you describe the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were wearing camouflage uniforms and black, most of them were black, and the men who wore them had stockings over their face and others did not have anything on their faces, and others had a lot of paint on their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the soldiers close enough to you that you could see whether or not they had any patches or emblems on their uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well no, perhaps I could see one or two HVO. They were HVO. As I would see them before, some of our neighbours wore them, so I could see some HVO patches. It seems to me it was yellow all around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask Mr. Dubuisson to show the witness what is already in evidence, exhibit number 100/2. Could you just put it on the ELMO, please? Is that the emblem that you saw those soldiers wearing and if not, could you describe what is different about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what the difference is. I know the HVO letters well and the chess board sign. How it was turned, I do not know, I am not very familiar with that and I never paid much attention to it, but at first sight, this is what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Could I just have the aerial photograph put back on the ELMO? Ms. Dedic, you said that at some point in time some soldiers came to the house where you were with your husband and your sons and had a conversation with your husband. Can you describe what that soldier was wearing, the one that had the conversation with your husband in front of your son's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see what these soldiers were wearing. I was not really there, there were a lot of boards out there, a lot of wood, about ten cubic metres, so I could not see my house, my son's house properly. I could only see the road, but from the wood, I could not see my son's house and I could not see what they were doing in front of my son's house. I did not have a good view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, perhaps you misunderstood what point in time I was talking about. You said at some point in time you were in the house and soldiers came to the house and called your husband outside. I believe you said you followed him out and he had the conversation with the soldier. Do you remember what uniform the soldier was wearing at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what you are referring to. I did not look very carefully and I could not see it, because as I was told to unlock the door, I had to go to my own house to get the key and then go and unlock the door, so I did not look very carefully. I just saw them in passing, but I did not even look at those who were right in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You said that your husband and your son did possess some pistols and had the pistols in the house that day, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband had a pistol for 20 years. It was privately owned and he had a licence, he bought it himself, and my son was a forestry worker and he had a pistol issued to him by the forest company he worked for. Also we had a burglary some time in the autumn, so my husband's pistol was stolen, but my son's pistol was still there. It was taken away from us, you know, how should I call this, this was the local community of the HVO, ours was taken and Islam's was taken, and then they gave it back in a day or two. I know these neighbours of ours who took it away from us and then they gave these pistols back to us in a day or two, but I cannot remember their names. Also we had some kind of rifle, maybe you know about this case, you know, people would bring parts of rifles and then make rifles out of them. My younger son was fond of shooting, for example, at weddings when people were having a good time and the younger boy said, "daddy, could I do a bit of shooting?", so he was shooting between the two houses and he hit a telephone wire. A man came from the road and he asked my husband, "who was shooting just now?" , and he said, "Haris". That rifle remained in our house that night and then these neighbours, these Croat neighbours of ours took it away from us afterwards, but now five years later, I cannot remember their names. I knew their names then, though, they were the sons of a man who lived pretty far away from us, about half a kilometre away from us and they never gave it back to us. It was a very plain rifle, we had assembled it ourselves. I do not know whether you know about the case of the military barracks, when it exploded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, you do not need to go into all the detail of the history of the rifle. I just need to establish, on that morning, 16th April, did your husband or son still have that rifle in the house? Yes or no, did they have that rifle in the house that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can corroborate that, no. These neighbours took it away from us. I do not know their names now, I knew them before, these two brothers, they were going from one house to another and taking things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine. You said however that your son Haris did have a pistol. Did he give that pistol to the soldiers when they came to the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As Hadisa came to our door, at that very moment he had the pistol in his hands, Hadisa Pezer, he said, "are they looking for arms?", and she said, "regardless of whether you give them the gun or not, regardless of whether you want it over to them or not, they are going to kill you, that is what my Fadil did too". I do not know what kind of gun Fadil had. It was some kind of a hobby, you know. A lot of people had pistols there. As far as I know, quite a few neighbours had pistols, but they had licences too, you can check on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At any point in time on that day, 16th April, did you see your son or husband fire that pistol at any of the soldiers or men coming toward your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not even try. That is where we lived and it is in the middle of a field, you cannot really shoot. How can a father and a son start shooting these masses of people? They handed over the gun immediately to the first man who walked in and what they did with the pistol later I do not know, but they gave it to the first man who walked in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then you said, I believe you said you had gone and unlocked the garage and going into the garage, you saw the soldiers leading your son Fariz away, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Fariz, the older one is Fariz and the younger one is Haris. So the older one was married for a year and a half and he had a six month old baby. This soldier took him behind the garage, and he held a gun to his back and he took him to the house of Munib Ribo, my sister's house, and Munib had just arrived and his wife too and then I arrived to my son's house and my husband was there and the wife and the three little girls walked in to the garage. How much time did it take, 20 or 30 minutes for all of us to be assembled there, all of us from these houses, but it was pretty fast. When Munib arrived, then the same soldier went to Siljak Adem, this was my brother and he called him and said, "uncle, get out, these soldiers are looking for you and they are not going to do you any harm. You and Hatka and the children should come over to our garage. Father and Munib are already there in front of the garage, so come on", and he went on, he went to the house of Nesib Ahmic, this same soldier, so they went up there and they brought Nesib's wife to the garage and his daughter and his son Elvedin and Elvedin's wife, whereas Nesib was somewhere at work and the other son Dzevad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you just a moment. Would it be correct to say that you learned that your son Fariz, after he went around the garage, that he went basically from house to house of your neighbours and family and called the men out of those houses, is that essentially what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When we started talking in the garage, Hatka, my daughter-in-law, she came into the garage wounded. Fariz brought her there, but Hatka, as she was getting into my garage, she was wounded, and Adem Siljak, my brother, and my son were not allowed to go in front of Fariz's house, we did not see them after that, so they crossed this field and they went towards Islam's yard. These other soldiers from there were saying, "come here, the two of you", so they went there and we did not see them in front of my house any more, or in front of my son's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, did you learn that your son Fariz was killed that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were locked up, we realised that they had been killed. We heard bursts of strong gunfire and then it became very silent. I always talk very fast. When the Hrjnics were getting into the garage and Haris, they kept saying, "all your houses are on fire and all your men are killed in front of Fariz's house". They saw it as they were coming in. They came into the garage perhaps ten minutes after us or five minutes after us. They were brought into my yard later and that is when they told us, Samija and Haris Hrjnic, they said, "Munib is lying dead by the wood and your Mujo is lying beneath the walnut tree, lying on his back". At 4.00, when we got out of the garage, these other women were turning around, but I did not turn around at that point in time, but I saw then immediately my husband's foot, he had slippers on his feet while he was in the house and I turned my head, I could not look, and at that point in time, around 4.00, as we were getting out of the house, I saw his foot, the foot of my dead husband, and I recognised the slippers because I know that when he walked into the house, he wore those slippers and he enjoyed wearing slippers when he was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so would it be correct to say that both your son Fariz and your husband Mustafa were killed on 16th April 1993, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were killed, exactly. I saw my husband's foot, I saw him dead that day, not after that. When these corpses were collected all over Ahmici, I do not know who was doing it, UNPROFOR, I am not too sure, my brother is Adem Siljak, his name was out there at the board, and my son Ahmic Amir -- I mean Islam's son, and since Islam's son survived, he was about 18 at that time, then on that board, which was put up on the -- this list which was put up on the board down there, they thought that it was my son Fariz actually. I cannot remember all of this now, I know it was about 30 people. This man who was recognising people in old Vitez, Islam was his boss at Impregnancia and he enjoyed wearing some yellow shoes and also a special jacket. He recognised Islam's jacket and shoes and then he said that that was Islam Ahmic, he put him on the list, he identified him as such, so he was found in Islam's yard, and everybody thought it was Amir Ahmic in the yard, but because he survived, he got out alive together with us, his mother, when she went to Stari Vitez after about a year, she took him away from this list of the deceased and he was also supposed to do his military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to be sure that the court understands, is it your understanding that your son Fariz and that your husband are both buried in the Muslim cemetery in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think the judges have understood that point, Ms. Paterson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and the man who told us about it, to be very accurate, the man who was collecting the dead bodies, we asked, "what did Amir Ahmic wear at that time? What kind of clothes?". He had a leather jacket and leather boots and we asked about his sweater. He said, "do not ask me about his sweater or about his head, but he had a denim jacket and leather boots", that is exactly what my son wore that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you yourself saw Ado and Meho Hrjnic killed while you were in the garage. In addition to Ado and Meho, and your husband and son, how many other men were killed that morning in the area around your house and garage. You do not have to go into details about it, just how many men were killed and their names, if you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can, yes. Ado and Meho on the one side and my husband and Munib on the other side, they were about 20 metres away. Ado and Meho were killed a bit further up, right in front of the house, and Mujo, my Mustafa, and Munib Ribo, my brother-in-law, they were killed a bit lower, below the house, but to the other side of the wood, I do not know how to explain this to you, not right in front of the house, not right in the centre of the yard, because this wood was collected there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you know what total number of men were killed that morning? Was it nine men that were killed there in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me count. Ahmic Ado and Meho two, Munib and Mustafa four, Islam Ahmic and Elvedin Ahmic, and my son Fariz Dedic and Siljak Adem my brother. You do the counting. Two, four, six, eight. And the ninth was Sefik Ahmic, because he was killed down there about 100 or 200 metres away from them, in another part of the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. On 16th April, this same day, what happened to your house? Was your house damaged in any way and did you see it being damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were locked up in the garage, all these people were killed, all the houses were on fire, but this house of mine, we call it the new house and the old house, I do not know how you are going to take this, my son's house was the new house and the old house was the one where I lived. I saw two soldiers coming up, they wore helmets and they had a litre or two in plastic jerry cans and they walked into my house. My house was not on fire yet. All the other houses were already burning, so they were there a minute or two or ten minutes and then they went back and the house started burning and they went to the main road, which was nearby, they went to the main road, Zenica/Vitez, the Zenica/Vitez main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now could you continue your story and tell the judges what happened after you said you left the garage and were taken to another house nearby. Continue with your story, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can. We were in my garage until 4.00 and then this group moved to Nesib's weekend house, it was not a real house, the first floor was on fire and the top floor was not. Draze and Zoran Vrebac were there and that is where they stayed and that is where we spent the night, this group of us, all the way until the morning. In the morning, since Andjelko, Ivan's son, was around there, and Mirko's son, I forget his name, we saw their wives going from house to house, they were parallel house, 10 to 20 metres apart, and Seka, Nevenka, I forget the others, women's names, "come over here", we yelled, and they came to this garage and when we saw who was there and what was going on, she said, "what shall we do, shall we go?". Those three men had told us not to budge from there, but they came over round the fence and they came over. Then Jozo arrived and Ivan and Andjelko, I think that is what his name was. They helped us cross the road, they were sort of protection of some kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, look towards the judges, please. It is the judges who are going to be dealing with this case. There is no harm in you not being aware of that, these are events that did mark you, so we can understand that you can get caught up, but do continue and then there will be just a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Then we went over there to this Crisis Staff there and we stayed there the second night, because it was already dark by then and other groups were arriving, from Zume and up the main road. So it was like a collection centre, it was not just us from our neighbourhood, there were even women from the neighbourhood where the cemetery was.
