There were weekend houses there and so there were a lot of refugees there, so their woman folk arrived, so from Krcevine and we all came to this crisis centre, I think we were about 190 or something, and that is where we spent the second night.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, let me just ask you a couple of brief questions to clarify this part of your story. After you were in the garage, you were taken to the house of Nesib Ahmic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from my garage to Nesib's garage, and then to the Crisis Staff in Zume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If I can direct your attention to the aerial photograph in front of you, can you just tell the judges which letter represents Nesib Ahmic's house? Would that be letter F?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am going to turn a little bit so that I can follow the main road, it helps me. The garage is E and Nesib is letter F.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you were taken to the HVO Crisis Staff headquarters. What number is that on the diagram? Is that number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Across the street and up, up, yes. Up around here (indicates) there is the house of Pican's and then another one and then Danica's and then under number 3, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the Crisis Staff headquarters? How many days were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spent -- that be one whole day and night in this Crisis Staff headquarters, until about 8.00 or 9.00 in the morning, I do not know exactly what time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left the Crisis Staff headquarters? Where were you taken after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken in the direction to Dubravica, to the school building. It was an elementary school there and there we stayed 15 or 17 days. Over 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before we go on to the Dubravica school, while you were still at the HVO headquarters, was there an incident when some soldiers came and tried to take away your younger son, Haris?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was at the Crisis Staff headquarters in Zume on the second day. A soldier arrived, quite tall and dark, and he was saying, "the men who were collecting bodies should come out". We did not know who was going -- then Zenur came out, Amir his brother and a man named Munib, I do not know his name. Then when they were going out, he pointed to my son, to another man and to somebody from Loncari, then he also pointed at Hasim and his wife objected to that and he told her to shut up. She stepped forward towards him and I said, "please do not, you killed my brother, son, neighbours everybody, spare him please". This soldier said, "you be silent and if you are not silent I will kill both you and him". Then my son was silent there and he sat down. Then he again pointed at Hasim and took him away and those four men were never seen from that morning on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just briefly describe to the court what this man looked like, what he was wearing, the man who took these four men away that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had black clothes, outfit, it was -- I think they called them Jokers. He had a hat turned backwards and he also carried a weapon that was rare. I do not know about this Jokers, there was like -- he had like a stick and held it over our heads. We were at least 100 there in that room, because 30 came just from my garage, and then as the others joined the group, they were coming from Prijedor, there were even neighbours, there were some refugees, some women from those houses that were over on the cemetery side and Krcevine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, and you said that you spent 15 days at the Dubravica school. After that, were you eventually released from the school and left the area of Santici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After 15 days, we went and we were then taking care of ourselves. My daughter-in-law, my grandchild, my younger son and I took a bus and then went out and for a while we were in Norway, in a camp, and then spent another three months with a friend and now we have our own place.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Dedic. I have no further questions, I would just like to introduce some photographs. Ms. Dedic, we discussed this, as you will recall, before and I said I would leave it up to you. Would you like me to show you these photographs or would you just like me to introduce them directly to the court. These are photographs of your husband, your son and some other friends and relatives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could take a look at it. That is the reason why I brought them, so that I would have it too. These were the pictures from my son's wedding and I wanted to have these pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, I know your inclination is to look at these and talk about your family members, but if you would please look at the photographs and just identify who the people are in the photographs. If the court wants to ask you additional questions, they will do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I would gladly do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms. Dedic, it is for you to decide whether you want to identify these pictures or not. If you care to, do go right ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well, I will look at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then just very briefly, if you could tell us who the family members on these pictures are. I think we all have the same document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my husband, Mustafa, and this is my son Haris and this is my younger brother. That is it, it is over.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is Exhibit 146/1. The man on the right is your husband Mustafa and the man in the middle is your son Fariz, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next photograph, 146/2, could you just identify the men in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Mujo Ahmic, the godfather of my daughter-in-law, and he was also killed and the man with the moustache, this is Adem Siljak, my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, the man in the photograph in the white jacket?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mujo Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man with the moustache is your brother, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my brother Adem Siljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Next photograph, 146/3, the man in the moustache, is that your brother again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were killed -- yes, this is again Mujo Ahmic, this is also from the wedding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the man in that photograph who has his arm around your brother, that is your son Fariz, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Fariz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally the last photograph, 146/4, the man in the centre of the photograph with the red collar, that is your son Fariz, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the one who is holding the two fingers, and you can see him up in the corner, that is Elvedin Ahmic and his name is also in Stari Vitez. He is Nesib Ahmic's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the man in the far right of the photograph, you can only see half his face, he is holding up his hand, he was also killed, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Dedic. Mr. President, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nobilo? Cross-examined by MR. NOBILO

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will attempt to be quite short. Good evening, madam Dedic. You see we already have the evening upon us and I am the Defence counsel for General Blaskic, together with my colleague Mr. Russell Hayman. I only have a couple of questions for you. When Islam Ahmic your neighbour told you he was hit, were there any HVO soldiers around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were approaching like this (indicates). As I said before, I do not know the distance, 20 or 30 metres from the corner of his house and I do not know how else to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at what distance were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20, 30 metres, I really could not tell you, but they were spread out like this (indicates), so they were coming this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Islam Ahmic, was he a member of the TO or the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe he was. He travelled with my husband, he worked in Impregnancia and he also was on work duty, he was a foreman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a pistol, private, just like my husband. Where he kept it that morning, I do not know, we never talked about it, but I know I can say this, that when my husband's pistol was taken away, his was taken away too and then was returned to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so. He was laughing at our neighbours and our children. He was joking about this rifle that we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, is it true that Nenad Santic guaranteed the safety to your husband and your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Nenad Santic has a brother who was a great friend with my husband. He was a merchant in Vitez. They would meet often and they were friends, this brother of his, but I knew Nenad very little, I do not know him at all, but I know the brother quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can slow down a little bit for interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well, I just naturally speak very fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear about Nenad Santic? Was he an important person in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was often talked about. I heard stories from my neighbours, he was some kind of a commander and I would see him often as a neighbour. He lived down from us. We did not exchange visits but we were not hating each other either. But I knew his brother well. Him I knew much less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When the soldier arrived and talked to your husband and son and asked them, "did you watch television last night, that people were killed in Zenica and that is why the Muslims are being killed", do you remember that conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not, because I did not have enough time. He stayed there, I only heard these words at the moment when I was passing my husband. I heard him say, when my husband said, "by God, people, what is this", this is what I heard of this dark young man, "well, this is for what had happened in Zenica", and what happened in Zenica; believe it or not, I was not following television programmes that much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam Dedic, I will read you a fragment of what you said in your statement. I will read it in English and you will get it in interpretation. This is on page 2 of the witness statement: "My son was close there too. The soldiers said this is for what you saw on TV last night. Because you killed our people at the Zenica blockade, now we are killing your people." Is that what you stated to the investigators when you spoke to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, this was five years ago and I gave a statement even in the court in Zenica, and if there are discrepancies, I do not know how we can correct that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a better memory now than five years ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, that. I do not know, I am not sure myself. It was five years. I cannot recall every detail and every word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. When you came to the garage, what time was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you that, because when the shooting started, it was 5.15, 5.30, I was not looking at the watch. I do not know how much it took me to wake up my husband, maybe a minute or two, and then when I went to my son's house, I do not know, five or ten minutes, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am interested in something else now. You said that there was something in Slimane and then they got the rifles.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can tell you this. It was a warehouse of the JNA. I was told that this existed there before and the word got around the village that this depot blew up or something and maybe two days later, people went over there in cars, we had vehicles there, let us go and see what is up there. They collected some barrels and then they were making, putting them together, makeshift rifles, I do not know. But I know that they were doing this in my back yard, specially my young son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that only your son or were there other people doing this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I know about my son. They got these barrels, I do not know who he got it from. I do not know if it was somebody who went there in their car. I was not paying that much attention, but they were working on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did many people go in their cars to Slimane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I did not like to leave my house, my house is at the end of the commune and we are closer to Santici than to Ahmici, so I did not go much to upper Ahmici to people who lived around the mosque. I would only go there if there were something, some funeral or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your father shot at the telegraph pole, was there any damage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was telephone lines, a temporary makeshift line to my son's new house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took the pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know who these people from the local commune in Santici were. I know them, I know their faces but not their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Islam's son who was misidentified as your son who was killed, how was he rescued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, but that morning he was standing next to his father, Islam was there, Mijda and Amir, Mirza, I do not know. Every woman in Ahmici has her own story and I know that they will all come and tell it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were leaving the garage, you said it was around 4.00 in the afternoon. Can you tell me, was there any shooting going on around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were in the garage, and indeed the whole time the next day, when we were being taken in the direction to this one location, the shooting was going on towards Sljivcica, Ahmici and as we were passing we were talking to each other, we were saying "they are shooting", and that was over up above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was shooting going on both when you were in the garage and when you left it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we were in the garage we could hear again coming from the upper ground, something like shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the Crisis Staff headquarters, what you said to the Prosecutor was that other women arrived. What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Muslim women, but there was also a neighbour called Ljube, Karlovca, I think. She came in, she asked if we needed anything. Gavrinica also arrived. I guess her husband's name was Gavro. Some other women also arrived and I really did not take anything from them, because I had a six month old and I had to take care of her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were Croat women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any shooting going on around the Crisis Staff headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was silent, it was already dark. I cannot tell you whether there was any shooting or not, but believe it or not, in this plight that I was in, I was not paying much attention to anything except for this small baby of six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, thank you very much madam. Mr. President, I have completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I have no further questions, I would just like to take this opportunity to move into evidence Exhibits 145 and 146, 145 being the photo enlargement and the accompanying legend and 146 being the four photographs of Ms. Dedic's family members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. I have consulted my fellow judges, we deem to have heard sufficient information. Madam, we hope that your life is going to be happy in the future. Would you care to add something, madam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just wish to apologise to you, because I was under this face protection so I did not think that I had to pay that much attention to you, I did not have to look at you carefully, but I did not mean any offence. My only wish is -- that is what I wish to say, but I am a fast speaker naturally and I was afraid I would be speaking too fast, but may I just say that I hope that the evil that happened in Ahmici will never happen again anywhere in the world and my only hope is that nobody experiences it any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we all hope the same thing. Please do not move for the time being. The court is adjourned and will resume its proceedings tomorrow at 10.00. (5.30 pm)

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
